newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends up 25 cts, Brent trades 24 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends up 25 cts, Brent trades 24 cts.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed up 25 cents on Friday, posting a lame performance that barely managed to track stronger Brent and U.S. heating oil, traders said.
Front month April gas oil settled at $169.50 a tonne, 50 cents shy of the high and 75 cents off the low after moving in a narrow $1.25 range.
"It was very quiet. Gas oil followed Brent up but if anything the increase lagged behind crude's rise," a trader said.
It's well supplied and although there is some cold weather about it just wasn't enough to provide support," he added.
April Brent futures were up 25 cents at $20.14 a barrel at 1758 GMT. May was up 23 cents at $190.65.
Traders said crude's gains originated in jockeying for positions ahead of the expiry of the April contract.
NYMEX heating oil was up 68 cents at 54.95 cents a gallon.

The April/May spread on IPE Brent has ballooned out to 49 cents, compared with just a few cents at one point earlier in the week. Spreads further forward were also wider, with May/June out at around +12 cents compared with seven or eight yesterday.
Markets rose on Thursday after news that April's Brent loading programme would be eight cargoes lighter than March.
Traders said the strength on Friday was partly a follow-through from that.
